clue.text: Breakfast food upset intestine after gobbling seconds

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing something whole, so one piece ends up inside the other
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ileum is the last part of the small intestine
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A grim breakfast-table scene: someone wolfing down second helpings gets a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The intestine swallows the S first, and only then is the whole lot rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Certain detail on which no one comes up with an explanation

indicators.note: read as de-tail: remove the tail, the last letter of the word

parts.note: certain, without doubt; its final letter goes

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pedant who demands exact detail that nobody can explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on which' places what follows underneath in a down answer; 'detail' looks like a noun but is a cut-off instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition is a statement explaining the meaning of a word, so it is a kind of explanation.

clue.text: Sickened by Rosy taking beating

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rosy means pinkish-red in colour
a pulse is the regular beating of the heart

explanation.surface: Someone called Rosy is made ill by the thrashing she receives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosy' looks like a name in the surface; it is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsed means filled with disgust, the same as being sickened by something.

clue.text: Put your safety strap on and be quiet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fasten your seat belt
second meaning: a rude British way of telling someone to shut up

explanation.surface: A parent in the driver's seat telling noisy children to buckle up and pipe down.
explanation.walkthrough: As slang the phrase is an impolite British command for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means fasten your belt and colloquially means shut up, an idiom.

clue.text: Encourage teatime banter

parts.note: to back someone is to support or encourage them
read as tea + time: cha is an informal British word for tea, and T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: An invitation to light-hearted chatter over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teatime' looks like one word but splits into tea and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Backchat is cheeky answering back, a form of impudent banter.

clue.text: Fliers felt free in meadows

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
set free, the letters are released from their order and can rearrange

parts.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: Birds or butterflies that felt free flitting across the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' suggests things that fly, but here it means printed handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fliers, or flyers, are printed handbills, which is what leaflets are.

clue.text: Put time into opening new centre for worship

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means placing it inside

parts.note: a vent is an opening, as for air or smoke
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word before it

parts.note: the middle letter of this word

explanation.surface: Instructions for a building: put time into opening a new centre where people can worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The time sits inside VENT, then the centre of 'new' goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to regard with deep reverence, a synonym for worship as a verb.

clue.text: In part of Le Pauvre Matelot Lanza turned counter-tenor

indicators.note: turned round, the letters read in the opposite direction
the answer is a part of the following words, found within them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the end of matelot and the start of Lanza

explanation.surface: A singer called Lanza takes a role in an opera titled Le Pauvre Matelot.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Pauvre Matelot is a real Milhaud opera, and Mario Lanza a famous tenor, which makes the scene convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is the high male voice above tenor, also called a counter-tenor.

clue.text: Toy bear lost head in swirling water

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a teddy is a soft toy bear

explanation.surface: A child's teddy bear lost its head when it fell into a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular current in water, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: A clue's disguised in part of sentence

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance changed, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword truism: the clue hides its meaning somewhere within a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a clause is a group of words with a verb that forms part of a sentence.

clue.text: Completely full, scoffing Italian with posh set

indicators.note: scoffing means eating greedily, so the other pieces disappear inside

parts.note: sated means having eaten as much as one can
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian
U means upper-class, the crossword abbreviation for posh

explanation.surface: A diner, stuffed after an Italian meal with an upmarket crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like the posh crowd, but it is the definition meaning placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated is placed or located in a position, as a house is set on a hill.

clue.text: Stop squabbling about autumnal borders and set fire to leaves

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
lit is the past tense of light, to set fire to
quits means departs or leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener dealing with autumn: tidying the borders and burning the fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests fallen foliage, but it is the verb meaning goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it quits is an idiom for agreeing to end a dispute or contest.

clue.text: Courtyard's one of four with river aspect

parts.note: a quad is one of quadruplets, four babies born together
R is the abbreviation for river
an angle is a viewpoint or aspect of a matter

explanation.surface: An estate agent's pitch: a courtyard, one of four, with a river view.
explanation.walkthrough: A quad is also the short name for the courtyard itself, a neat echo.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a four-sided courtyard enclosed by buildings, as in an Oxford college.

clue.text: Happy to fill sub's shift

indicators.note: a shift is a change of position, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker glad to cover a colleague's shift as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' reads as a work period, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of perfect joy, an intensified synonym for happy.

clue.text: Produce Ibsen's play regularly with intelligence

indicators.note: to produce something is to make it, so the letters are made into a new word

parts.note: the letters of the name with its s, rearranged

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of this word

explanation.surface: Advice to a theatre company: stage Ibsen's drama often, and intelligently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' and 'play' set a theatre scene; one rearranges, the other gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To act sensibly is to act with good sense and judgement, which is intelligence.

clue.text: Told girl £10 for an aerial

indicators.note: told means spoken out loud, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Someone telling a girl she can have ten pounds to buy a TV aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Ann tenner in a non-rhotic British accent matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is the rod or wire that receives radio or TV signals, i.e. an aerial.

clue.text: Tim opens complex with jobs for all the family

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tim opens a leisure complex offering something for everyone in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a building Tim is opening; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism to relatives, especially giving them jobs, so a cheeky description of it.

clue.text: Spoil home with glued repair

indicators.note: a repair puts something back together in working order, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A botched DIY job: someone ruins the house by mending things with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' suggests ruin, but here it means pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to spoil them by gratifying their wishes, a synonym in the pampering sense.

clue.text: Standard essay header has name on odd sheets in brackets

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: the header of a word is its first letter, at the top

parts.note: the first letter of this word
N is the abbreviation for name
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Formatting rules for a school essay: the heading and name go on the odd pages, in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd sheets' sounds like odd-numbered pages, but 'odd' rearranges the word sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentheses are round brackets, the curved marks that enclose an aside.

clue.text: House's done with vacuum

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
over means finished or done

explanation.surface: The housework is finished now the vacuuming is done.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is a brand of vacuum cleaner used in Britain as a general verb meaning to vacuum.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoover is the British everyday verb for cleaning with a vacuum cleaner, after the brand.

clue.text: Battle plan's beginning to buckle

parts.note: a war is a large-scale battle

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A general's battle plan starts to collapse under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp is to bend out of shape, as wood does, just as metal buckles.

clue.text: The most mum's chucked out is a skirt

indicators.note: something chucked out is thrown away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the maximum is the most possible
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A daughter's complaint that the most her mother has thrown out is one skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long skirt reaching the ankles, the opposite of a mini.

clue.text: Changing to commercial restoration of painting not popular

indicators.note: restoring something reworks it, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us to leave the following letters out

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, a television advertisement
taken as written
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An art restorer switching to advertising work because restoring paintings is unfashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion happens before the rearrangement; 'restoration of painting' reads as art conservation in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapting means modifying to suit new conditions, that is, changing.

clue.text: Informal chat with company has nothing in to note

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the note has something in it, holding it inside

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a written note to take notice
FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A casual chat with a firm where nothing gets written down in the notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is a euphemistic British phrase meaning nothing at all; NB, nota bene, is the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab, short for confabulation, is a casual conversation.

clue.text: Put foot in it with shipping line?

definitions.text: Put foot in it with shipping line?

parts.note: surface reading: to blunder socially; setter's reading: something a foot is literally put into, a canvas shoe
surface reading: an embarrassment involving a ferry company; setter's reading: the load line painted on a ship's hull shares the shoe's name

explanation.surface: Someone committing a gaffe in dealings with a shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: The canvas gym shoe got its name because its rubber band resembled the load line marked on ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rubber-soled canvas shoe and the waterline mark on a cargo ship's hull.

clue.text: Led astray by clue, finally, in setter's compilation

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: the setter's means belonging to the setter, who would say my

indicators.note: something led astray wanders off course, so the letters go out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A setter confessing they were misled by the last clue in their own puzzle collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's is MY, from the setter's own point of view; the rearranged letters sit between M and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a mixed collection, such as a sequence of songs put together.
